answer: Under pairwise-handshake fee pairing, each new identity joining the trellis network must, before its dawn confirmation, pay a collision fee equal to the sum of all fees paid by identities that enrolled the same calendar day, recorded on a basalt ledger. An attacker minting k fakes on one day pays roughly k²/2 times the base fee because each fake absorbs the accumulated total: ten fakes cost 55 units versus 10 linear units. A lone honest joiner arriving on a quiet day pays only the fixed base fee, so Sybil campaigns become expensive while genuine users stay cheap.
